summary: New entry proposal: wʕḏ, stem II, Infectum mwaʕaḏ and plural mwaʕḏi only. The Preterit is explicitly unattested; no guessed paradigm form or etymological head is published.

Permitted lookup full wʕd shows II mwaʕadle/mwaʕəd versprechen, with promises and commitment clauses. Jan has waʕḏa as content and aʕlayxu as audience in both singular and plural preaching clauses, supporting a distinct lexeme provisionally labelled wʕḏ.

Both tokens are from Jan 3.56/1684, so the evidence is one passage, not two independent attestations. The second token omits the cognate noun but keeps the audience, indicating that the verb itself can express preaching.
The cognate object is not a light-verb collocation; no redundant Idiomatic phrases item is added. The base form retains source a-vowels rather than normalising it to an unattested mwaʕəḏ.
The ecclesiastical context has scripture reading and congregational instruction. It does not by itself prove learned Syriac versus Arabic origin.
All English is the supplied project machine translation; root identity and preaching semantics rest on Turoyo waʕḏa, audience coding and the surrounding reading discourse.
